title: Cholesterol-lowering effects of dietary fiber: a meta-analysis
authors: Brown L, Rosner B, Willett WW, Sacks FM
journal: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
followUp: mean treatment 49 days (14 to 168); pectin trials mean 34 days (28 to 42)
population: 67 controlled trials in adults of oat products (25), psyllium (17), pectin (7) and guar gum (18), published 1966 to June 1996
funder: not stated. The article gives affiliations (Harvard School of Public Health; Channing Laboratory, Brigham and Women's Hospital and Harvard Medical School) and thanks four individuals; it carries no funding statement. PubMed lists no grant support.
inKindSupport: One unpublished trial (Beling et al, 1991) was provided by Quaker Oats, Chicago.
result: Soluble fibre at 2-10 g/day was associated with total cholesterol -0.045 mmol/L per g (95% CI -0.054 to -0.035) and LDL cholesterol -0.057 mmol/L per g (-0.070 to -0.044); the effects of soluble fibre from oat, psyllium or pectin were not significantly different; triacylglycerols and HDL cholesterol were not significantly influenced. Pectin: 7 trials, 277 subjects, mean dose 4.7 g/day (2.2 to 9.0), mean 34 days; total cholesterol -0.070 mmol/L per g (-0.117 to -0.022); LDL cholesterol, 4 trials and 117 subjects, -0.055 mmol/L per g (-0.087 to -0.022).
